Same-form (duchess) entries: 4 SOLD at $55, $100, $120 and $210 (Nov 2025 to Sep 2026) plus 1 UNSOLD near twin (2 bids, passed in Sep 2026). No asking prices gathered. lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving same-form SOLD of comparable quality is $100 (437570, Sep 2026; $55 lot 372264 is a lesser 3 drawer piece so not used as the floor). 100 / 1.198 = 83.47, round down to $80 hammer ($95.84 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $150 (middle of $100 to $210 same-form SOLD hammers, ours is a better-carved 8 drawer example but has a damaged mirror clasp). Less about 10% selling cost ($15, local Marketplace or re-auction allowance), $0 postage (pickup furniture) = $135. 135 / 2.396 = 56.3, round down to $55 hammer. Margin is thin, so FLIP only works at the bottom of the range.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification from the photo and the Gowans title, and 4 same-form Gowans SOLD results whose API data and photos I checked. Not High: furniture carries no maker mark to read, and the mirror clasp damage (stated in title) is not visible, so condition is partly unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped outright. Reclassified 436116 from same item to category guide (pedestal dressing chest with detached mirror, not a duchess) and 384380 from close to category guide (chest of drawers with box mirror). Added 437570-type twins 364926 and 400221 as very close (both were already listed by the researcher). Note the lot is 468A in Gowans' data, not 468.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Good colour and high polish, carved acanthus scroll mirror supports intact, oval mirror plate looks clear, all small drawer knobs present, long drawer has two turned knobs, shaped platform base sound. Mirror clasp damage (in the title) not visible; the mirror pivot fixings cannot be seen. Polish may be a later refinish. Counting drawers: 3 + 3 small, 1 central, 1 long = 8, matching the title.
lots.condition: Looks good, possibly refinished; mirror clasp (pivot) damaged per Gowans title, extent unknown.
lots.question_for_gowans: How bad is the mirror clasp damage on lot 468A: is a pivot screw or bracket broken, does the mirror still tilt and hold its position, and is the mirror glass original and free of cracks or foxing? Any splits in the top or loose legs?
